pages.title: What Raises It
pages.text: Instability is born of three old sins: silence, contradiction, and greed. Sparse books, random vows, clashing commands, strange terrain, cruel weather, crowded biomes, and mighty landmarks all make an Age restless. Worst of all is losing the descriptive book itself. When the bound volume is truly destroyed or allowed to vanish, the Age suffers a savage wound of two hundred instability.

pages.title: What Lowers It
pages.text: A named thing is calmer than an unnamed one. Give the Age land, biomes, time, sun, moon, stars, and weather. A single biome is a lullaby. A familiar world-shape is another. Even danger behaves better when invited by name instead of arriving through accident.

pages.title: Effects
pages.text: Every Age keeps a hidden fever. When it rises, the first signs are weakness and ill luck. Then come lightning, blasts, and decay creeping like mold through reality. The rot may bloom black or white, for each Age chooses its own pallor.

pages.title: Curses
pages.text: Some wounds are not the fever itself, but one cruel phrase still caught in the script: endless storm, harmful enchantment, thin gravity, hostile surges, lifeless silence, locked time, or a starless sky. A linked descriptive book will name these on its survey once the Age is known.

pages.title: Cleansing
pages.text: Set the linked descriptive book in the $(thing)Editing Table$() with a $(item)Curse Cleansing$() symbol page, one ink vial, four lapis, and an amethyst shard. The table lifts the strongest legible curse first and eases a little instability, but sacrifices and careful writing still do the heavier healing.

pages.title: Control
pages.text: Those with steward's authority may speak $(thing)/mystcraft instability toggle$() while standing in an Age. This stills or wakes the symptoms for the whole family of that Age, lesser Nether and End included, but it does not lower the raw fever. The sickness remains beneath the skin.
